tier_reason: docs/resampler.html names libsamplerate but only says zita-resampler at its highest quality setting 'will be faster than most similar libraries providing the same quality, e.g. libsamplerate', with no numbers, workload or method; the only benchmark code in the repo (test/speedtest.cc, test/vspeedtest.cc) times zita alone (44100 -> 48000, input frames per second) with no baseline and no published results. No reachable source (SampleRateTap async/docs/COMPARISON.md, other GitHub copies, Ardour's vendored copy, nixpkgs packaging) carries a numeric comparison with libsamplerate or libsoxr, so the claim stays directional.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Directional only: 'Even at the highest quality setting libzita-resampler will be faster than most similar libraries providing the same quality, e.g. libsamplerate.' No numbers. Separately, the docs say the 1.8.0 SSE2 build 'will reduce CPU load by a factor of at least 2'; that factor is against the library's own scalar build, not against libsamplerate. The quality/CPU trade-off spans 'approximately 1:6' (CPU load roughly proportional to hlen).
corrections.workload: No benchmark workload behind the libsamplerate claim. The repo's test/speedtest.cc only times zita-resampler itself (44100 -> 48000 Hz, given channel count and hlen, input frames per second) with no baseline and no published results.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 35 stars, 5 forks (digital-stage GitHub copy). Upstream is packaged in nixpkgs (1.11.2), an older 2012 version is vendored in Ardour (libs/zita-resampler), and it is the resampler behind zita-ajbridge (named in the SampleRateTap comparison table).
corrections.caveats: Tier D: a first-party directional claim with no numbers. The repo is digital-stage's 2021 import (8 commits, 2021-02-16 to 2021-03-10, no releases, not a GitHub fork) of upstream release 1.8.0 by Fons Adriaensen; its sources, docs and README match 1.8.0 (version macros 1.8, copyright 2006-2020, AUTHORS Fons Adriaensen) with a CMake build added. The canonical upstream is https://kokkinizita.linuxaudio.org/linuxaudio/ (unreachable from this environment), which has moved on to at least 1.11.2 (nixpkgs bumped to it on 2025-06-04), so this copy is behind upstream and abandoned; upstream's own activity date could not be checked. The copy's CMakeLists.txt sets non-standard variables (CMAKE_CXXFLAGS_FLAGS, CMAKE_CPPFLAGS_FLAGS) that CMake ignores and never defines ENABLE_SSE2, so a CMake build of this copy gets the scalar path without -O2 unless the user adds flags; the 'factor of at least 2' SSE2 gain applies to the upstream Makefile build, which enables SSE2 by default. GPL-3.0-or-later copyleft (file headers say 'version 3 ... or any later version'; nixpkgs labels upstream 1.11.2 gpl3Only, not checked at source). The SampleRateTap comparison (now async/docs/COMPARISON.md) lists 'zita-resampler + zita-ajbridge' with 'no published CI-verified figures' and measures only libsamplerate, soxr and r8brain-free-src.

notes: Kept at D: copy verified as the upstream 1.8.0 release, and no numeric zita vs libsamplerate/libsoxr comparison exists in any reachable source (3 WebSearch queries, GitHub copies, SampleRateTap, Ardour, nixpkgs). Consider a repo_url override to the canonical upstream https://kokkinizita.linuxaudio.org/linuxaudio/ (current 1.11.2), since the digital-stage copy is a frozen 2021 import whose CMake build silently drops the SSE2 path.
